title: Re-allow legacy [file_str, revision_str] form on file-scoped commands
description:
T19 of the cursor-resolution refactor (see ~/.claude/plans/you-are-a-software-staged-kazoo.md Stage 6, ticket T21) removed legacy [file_str, revision_str] form from squash/unsquash. This broke Neovim CLI commands :JJSquash <file> @- and :JJUnsquash <file> @- in clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/commands.lua which forward args.fargs (a list of strings) directly to the server.

Fix: in server/src/commands.rs::resolve_file_and_revision_arg, drop the reject_string_arg call. Change either the resolver signature or its caller server/src/server.rs::resolve_file_scoped_args (line 109-120) so both args[0] and args[1] are passed in. If args[0] is Value::String(file) AND args[1] is Value::String(rev), return Ok((file, rev)); otherwise (args[0] is the cursor object) proceed with existing cursor-form resolution.

Affects: badjuju.squash, badjuju.unsquash.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test passes with zero warnings. server/src/commands.rs unit tests cover [file, revision] string-form happy path and cursor-form still works. server/tests/lsp.rs has lsp_execute_squash_string_args_return_error replaced with lsp_execute_squash_string_args_succeed (set up a touched file, send [file, '@-'], assert no error and the file no longer shows as modified). New lsp_execute_unsquash_string_args_succeed mirroring squash. Manual: with a modified file in the working copy, :JJSquash <file> @- and :JJUnsquash <file> @- round-trip cleanly in Neovim.
notes: Plan reference: ~/.claude/plans/you-are-a-software-staged-kazoo.md Stage 6 T21. Sibling: T20 revision-scoped (bad-juju-qv3). Independent of T20 — both can land in parallel. After both land, consider bd remember the invariant: revision-scoped resolvers accept BOTH string and cursor forms; do not reintroduce reject_string_arg.

title: Re-allow string-form revision arg on revision-scoped commands
description:
T19 of the cursor-resolution refactor (see ~/.claude/plans/you-are-a-software-staged-kazoo.md Stage 6, ticket T20) removed legacy string-form acceptance from revision-scoped server commands. This broke (a) Neovim CLI user commands like :JJDescribe @-, :JJEdit abc, :JJAbandon @-, :JJDiff @-, :JJRebase src dst, :JJBookmark create foo @ in clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/commands.lua which forward the user's typed string and have no cursor by construction; and (b) the commit-line code actions built by server/src/server.rs::commit_actions (line 122-155) which ship Value::String(revision) for badjuju.edit/abandon/describe/diff/new. The integration tests only assert action shape, never invocation, so (b) is a silent latent regression.

Fix: in server/src/commands.rs::resolve_revision_arg, drop reject_string_arg(arg)?, and at the top of the function if arg is Some(Value::String(s)) return Ok(s.to_string()); otherwise fall through to existing cursor-form resolution. Mirror the dual-acceptance pattern that resolve_log_shortcut_arg already implements. Delete reject_string_arg entirely if it ends up with no callers after T21.

Affects: badjuju.edit, badjuju.abandon, badjuju.describe, badjuju.diff, badjuju.new, badjuju.rebase (source only), badjuju.bookmark (revision only).
acceptance_criteria: cargo test passes with zero warnings. server/src/commands.rs unit tests cover string-form happy path and cursor-form still works. server/tests/lsp.rs has the existing lsp_execute_describe_string_arg_returns_error replaced with lsp_execute_describe_string_arg_succeeds, plus new lsp_execute_{edit,abandon,diff,new}_string_arg_succeeds, lsp_execute_rebase_string_args_succeed, lsp_execute_bookmark_string_args_succeed. lsp_code_action_on_log_commit_line_returns_seven_actions extended to actually invoke one direct-action command via workspace/executeCommand and assert no error. Manual: :JJDescribe @-, :JJEdit @-, :JJAbandon @-, :JJDiff @-, :JJRebase @- @--, :JJBookmark create scratch @ all succeed in Neovim. cmd+./<leader>a on a non-@ log commit line, select 'Edit commit X', edit applies.
notes: Plan reference: ~/.claude/plans/you-are-a-software-staged-kazoo.md Stage 6 T20. Sibling: T21 file-scoped. No client changes needed. The fix is purely server-side because the CLI fundamentally lacks a cursor position.

title: feat: ? help popup driven by single-source-of-truth keymap table
description: Foundation ticket for the new hotkey system. Today, bindings live in three disjoint places (clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/keymap.lua, clients/vscode/package.json, and server-rendered COMMAND REFERENCE text). They drift independently. Per the Neogit issue #619 cautionary tale (help popup shows hardcoded defaults instead of actual bindings), introduce a single source of truth that drives all three: hotkey registrations, the COMMAND REFERENCE block, and a new ? help popup.
design: Define a portable keymap-entry data structure on the server: { key, action (stable command-id), description, windows[] }. Group entries into per-profile, per-window tables; default profile is 'magit'. Server exposes a new LSP request badjuju/keymap returning the active profile's table; clients fetch on init. Replace STATUS_/LOG_/DIFF_COMMAND_REFERENCE constants in server/src/commands.rs with a renderer that derives the COMMAND REFERENCE block from the keymap table. Add badjuju.help LSP command. Neovim: ? opens a floating window listing active bindings for the current buffer's window-type. VS Code: ? opens a QuickPick listing active bindings, with each item invoking its command. Profile read from initializationOptions.keymapProfile (mirrors existing commandReference override mechanism). Validate against [magit, vim, none], fall back to magit with log_message warning on unknown. Existing CommandReference override stays as escape hatch but no longer primary driver.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing ? in any of the 4 windows opens a help popup listing current bindings (nvim floating window OR VS Code QuickPick). COMMAND REFERENCE block at the bottom of each generated file is rendered from the keymap table -- no hardcoded text in Rust constants. initializationOptions.keymapProfile='magit' is the default and produces at-or-above today's parity. Clients can still override commandReference for full custom text. cargo test passes; new tests cover keymap-table to rendered-text for at least the status window. Help-popup keys MUST be derived from the active table, never hardcoded (Neogit #619 lesson).
notes: Critical files: server/src/keymap.rs (new), server/src/commands.rs (replace REFERENCE constants), server/src/server.rs (add badjuju/keymap request + badjuju.help cmd), clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/keymap.lua (fetch table, register binds, install ? popup), clients/neovim/lsp/jujutsu.lua (remove hardcoded commandReference override), clients/vscode/src/extension.ts (fetch + register ? QuickPick), clients/vscode/package.json (Bad Juju: Show Hotkey Help palette command). This is the foundation -- ALL other hotkey tickets depend on it.

title: Fix command name collision between LSP auto-registration and extension
description:
The vscode-languageclient library auto-registers VS Code commands for each command in the server's executeCommandProvider.commands capability (see node_modules/.../executeCommand.js lines 47-55). The server declares 'badjuju.new' and 'badjuju.refresh' in COMMANDS. The extension manually registers commands of the same name, causing 'command badjuju.new already exists' errors when the extension activates.

The other commands work because the extension uses distinct names (badjuju.status.open, badjuju.describe.open, badjuju.log.open) that don't collide with the server-declared ones (badjuju.status, badjuju.describe, badjuju.log).

Fix: rename the extension's manually-registered commands to badjuju.new.open and badjuju.refresh.open for consistency with the other commands, and update keybindings/contributes.
close_reason: Renamed extension commands to badjuju.new.open and badjuju.refresh.open to avoid collision with LSP client auto-registration of server-declared executeCommandProvider.commands. Build and 36 tests pass.

title: test(server): integration tests for op-head watcher refresh
description:
Add integration tests for the op-head watcher to server/tests/lsp.rs (or a new sibling file). Tests run against real jj subprocesses (no mocks).

**Test cases**:

1. **External mutation propagates**: tempdir + `jj git init`, boot LSP, open status.jujutsu via `badjuju.status`. Run `jj new` externally via `std::process::Command`. After waiting ≥600ms, assert `.jj/badjuju/status.jujutsu` mtime advanced and content reflects the new change.

2. **Self-caused mutation does not double-refresh**: open status.jujutsu, run a mutation through the LSP (e.g. badjuju.new). Capture status.jujutsu mtime immediately after the command returns. Wait ≥600ms. Assert mtime is unchanged (watcher suppressed the re-render).

3. **Status only refreshed when open**: do NOT open status.jujutsu. Run an external jj mutation. After ≥600ms, assert `status.jujutsu` does NOT exist on disk (`open_status_uri` was None → watcher skipped regeneration).

4. **Failed mutation does not record op**: simulate a failing mutation (e.g. squash with no parent). Assert `self_caused_ops` has no entry (errors short-circuit before recording).
acceptance_criteria:
- All 4 test cases pass
- Tests use tempdir + real jj subprocess (no mocks)
- Timing: ≥600ms wait to cover 500ms debounce plus margin
- `cargo test` passes with no warnings

title: feat(server): op-head filesystem watcher with 500ms debounce
description:
Add a filesystem watcher on `.jj/repo/op_heads/heads/*` that auto-refreshes open badjuju buffers when jj operations happen outside the LSP server.

**Dependency change** (server/Cargo.toml):
- Add `notify-debouncer-mini = "0.4"`
- Remove the unused `watchman_client` dep
- Drop the Watchman prereq line from README.adoc (~L121)

**Watcher initialization** (server/src/server.rs, in `initialize` alongside the `sweep_stale_diff_files` call ~L378):
- Resolve `<workspace_root>/.jj/repo/op_heads/heads/`
- If directory does not exist: log and skip, do not fail initialize
- Build debounced watcher with 500ms debounce, watching non-recursively
- Spawn a tokio task consuming debounced events
- Hold a `tokio::sync::Notify` (or oneshot) in `Backend` to signal shutdown on `Backend::shutdown`

**On each debounced event**:
1. Call `Jj::op_head_id()` to get the current op-head ID
2. Take a write-lock on State; call `take_if_self_caused(&op_id)`
3. If self-caused: log the suppression and return
4. Otherwise: call `Backend::refresh_open_artifacts(&jj, &workspace)`

Edge cases:
- `op_head_id()` returns Err → log and skip (don't crash the watcher task)
- `op_heads/heads/` deleted while watching → log and continue, don't panic

Watcher task holds clones of `Arc<RwLock<State>>` and `Client`.
acceptance_criteria:
- notify-debouncer-mini added to Cargo.toml; watchman_client removed
- Watchman prereq removed from README.adoc
- Watcher is spawned in initialize after workspace_root is set
- 500ms debounce window is used
- External jj mutation causes open status/log/diff buffers to refresh within ~600ms
- In-server mutation does NOT cause a second refresh
- Watcher task does not panic on op_head_id error
- `cargo test` passes with no warnings
- `redo check` passes

title: feat(server): track open status/log URIs in State; add refresh_open_artifacts
description:
Add explicit per-artifact URI tracking to `State` so the op-head watcher knows exactly which buffers are open and needs refreshing.

**State changes** (server/src/server.rs):
```rust
open_status_uri: Option<String>,
open_log_uri: Option<String>,
// open_diffs: HashMap<String, DiffTarget> already exists
```

Populate in `did_open` by filename match: URI ending in `/status.jujutsu` sets `open_status_uri`; URI ending in `/log.jujutsu` sets `open_log_uri`. Clear in `did_close` by URI equality. Keep `documents: HashMap<...>` untouched (it serves a different purpose).

**New method**: `Backend::refresh_open_artifacts(&self, jj: &Jj, workspace: &Path)`
1. Read-lock State; snapshot open_status_uri, open_log_uri, open_diffs presence
2. If open_status_uri is Some → call `commands::run_status(jj, workspace)`
3. If open_log_uri is Some → call `commands::regenerate_log_if_present(jj, workspace)`
4. Call `self.refresh_open_diffs(jj, workspace)` (existing method)

The inline post-command refresh paths in `execute_command` keep their current explicit sequences unchanged — `refresh_open_artifacts` is the watcher's dedicated entry point.
acceptance_criteria:
- State has `open_status_uri` and `open_log_uri` fields
- did_open sets the correct field by URI suffix match
- did_close clears the field when the matching URI closes
- `refresh_open_artifacts` runs jj status only when `open_status_uri` is Some
- `refresh_open_artifacts` runs log regen only when `open_log_uri` is Some
- `refresh_open_artifacts` always calls `refresh_open_diffs`
- Inline command refresh paths are not changed
- `cargo test` passes with no warnings

title: feat(server): track self-caused op-ids in State
description:
Extend `State` in server/src/server.rs with a `self_caused_ops: HashMap<String, Instant>` field to track op-ids caused by bad-juju itself. This lets the op-head watcher suppress double-refreshes when bad-juju runs a mutating jj command.

fix(neovim): status buffer doesn't auto-refresh after squash/unsquash
description:
After pressing `s` (squash) or `U` (unsquash) on a file in the status buffer, the buffer continues to show stale content until the user presses `R`. The server correctly rewrites `status.jujutsu` on disk before responding, but the Neovim `execute()` callback uses `:e!` to reload it, which silently fails because `status.jujutsu` is non-modifiable (`modifiable=false` set by ftplugin/jujutsu.lua). The `pcall` swallows the E21 error. VS Code is unaffected — it has a FileSystemWatcher that fires on every disk write.

## Context
Root cause: init.lua:168 calls `pcall(vim.cmd, 'silent! edit!')` after every command. On non-modifiable buffers, `:e!` fails with E21 and pcall discards the error. The describe-save flow already uses `:checktime` + autoread and works correctly. The fix is to replace `edit!` with `checktime` in the execute() callback — checktime respects autoread=true (set by ftplugin for all jujutsu buffers) without requiring modifiable=true. This also fixes the same silent no-op in badjuju.undo, badjuju.abandon, badjuju.new, badjuju.next, badjuju.prev.
design:
In `clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/init.lua` (~line 168), replace:

  pcall(vim.cmd, 'silent! edit!')

with:

  pcall(vim.cmd, 'checktime')

checktime polls all open buffers for on-disk changes. Combined with autoread=true (ftplugin/jujutsu.lua:16), it reloads any jujutsu buffer whose backing file changed — without requiring modifiable=true. Idempotent and cheap when nothing changed.
acceptance_criteria: 1. After squash (`s`), the status buffer immediately removes the squashed file — no R needed. 2. After unsquash (`U`), the status buffer immediately adds the file — no R needed. 3. badjuju.undo and badjuju.abandon also auto-refresh. 4. describe.jujutsu save still triggers status refresh (existing flow unchanged). 5. `redo check` passes.

title: plan how to have different hotkeys on different editors. the hotkey reference is created by the server so something needs to change
description:
The server hardcodes STATUS_COMMAND_REFERENCE, LOG_COMMAND_REFERENCE, and
DIFF_COMMAND_REFERENCE in server/src/commands.rs. These are appended to the
generated .jujutsu files so the user sees the hotkeys in-buffer.

Problem: hotkeys differ between clients.

VS Code-only keys (currently shown to all users):
  Ctrl+n        jj next
  Ctrl+p        jj prev
  Ctrl+Shift+n  jj next --edit
  Ctrl+Shift+p  jj prev --edit
  Ctrl+K U      unsquash alternative for vim-mode users

Neovim doesn't ship those bindings, so neovim users see misleading help text
inside the status buffer.

Single-letter keys (g r n l d u = q a s U) are common to both clients and
shouldn't need per-client overrides.
design:
## Options considered

### A. Client sends override references via initializationOptions (RECOMMENDED)
Client passes commandReference: { status, log, diff } in init_options.
Server stores them in State, uses them when rendering, falls back to built-in
defaults when absent.

Pros:
- Server stays editor-agnostic
- Each client controls its own help text without server changes
- Backwards compatible — older clients that don't send anything still work

Cons:
- Each client duplicates its keymap labels (already true for actual keymaps)
- Small refactor to thread references through run_status / run_log / run_diff
  (or via a Config struct passed alongside &Jj/&Path)

### B. Server picks by client name
Server reads clientInfo.name from initialize params, picks a hard-coded
reference per client.

Pros:
- One source of truth in the server

Cons:
- Tight coupling — adding a new client means a server release
- clientInfo.name is set by the LSP client and isn't a stable identifier
- Defeats the point of per-client customization

### C. Drop the reference from the server entirely
Each client renders its own help text and appends it post-server.

Cons:
- Requires the client to re-read and rewrite the file (or intercept the URI)
- Race conditions if the server rewrites the file mid-edit
- Significantly more complex client code

### D. Keyless reference (use verbs not keys)
Replace "n  new change" with "new change — see your editor's keymap".

Cons:
- Strictly worse UX; users currently rely on the in-buffer cheatsheet

## Recommended: Option A

## Implementation outline

1. server/src/server.rs: parse commandReference object from initializationOptions
   (each of status/log/diff optional). Store in State.
2. server/src/commands.rs: refactor run_status / run_log / run_diff to accept
   an optional reference override. Threading via &CommandReference struct is
   cleaner than three Option<&str> params.
3. clients/vscode/src/extension.ts: pass commandReference in initializationOptions.
   Default keeps current VS Code-flavored text.
4. clients/neovim/lsp/jujutsu.lua: pass commandReference in init_options.
   Drop the Ctrl+n/Ctrl+p/Ctrl+Shift lines; describe neovim-actual bindings.
5. Tests:
   - server: assert custom reference shows up in rendered files; assert default
     is used when init option absent.
   - vscode/neovim: integration tests that the right reference renders.

## Migration / compatibility

- The defaults in the server stay matching the VS Code-flavored text so older
  vscode clients that don't pass commandReference are unaffected.
- Neovim ships a populated commandReference from day one of this feature.
